scope: Static review of the exact private profile-only packet assembly and Kaggle code-file transport; no wrapper execution, provider call, fit, prediction export, or score.
findings: Independent rehash confirms all 15 packet files match the assembly receipt's names, byte sizes, and SHA-256 values. The assembly receipt, controller admission, and independent source-review receipt also match their cited hashes; packet external_review.json is byte-identical to the controller admission and packet_meta.json binds that same digest.

The embedded ZIP is decoded from the wrapper's literal constant without importing or executing the wrapper. Its SHA-256 matches both the wrapper constant and assembly receipt. It contains exactly 14 unique members; every member is a safe relative regular file with no absolute path, parent traversal, backslash, or symlink, and every member's bytes/hash match the packet directory and assembly map.

Static AST/source inspection confirms the Kaggle code entrypoint is the self-contained profile_kernel_bundle.py, whose imports are standard-library modules plus the dynamic profile_worker import after extraction. It verifies the embedded ZIP digest, uses a fresh extraction directory with exist_ok=False, rejects unsafe paths/symlinks, checks each embedded member digest, then adds the extracted packet root before importing profile_worker. There is no sibling-import regression in the selected code_file path.

The packet metadata is private and points to the exact E520 Profile V6 slug. The packet remains profile-only: fit, checkpoint, prediction export, and scoring are disabled. The controller admission separately preserves fresh pre-push quota/reserve, packet-hash, runtime, input-identity, and resource gates.
admission_effect: Static transport review passes for these exact packet bytes only. It does not itself submit or start the provider job; any push remains subject to the operator's fresh pre-push quota/reserve, target identity, runtime, input, and resource gates. It does not authorize fitting, scoring, or prediction export.
